His reign was one of significant changes for Tikal, including the adoption of some Teotihuacan styles, the probable subjugation of Tikal by Teotihuacan, and the possible presence of Teotihuacan warriors in Tikal. During this period, the art style began to reflect more of a Teotihuacan influence.
Yax Nuun Ahiin (also called "Curl Snout") came to the throne in 378 and ruled for 42 years. He is thought to have been an immigrant from Teotihuacan and his arrival marks the beginning of a period of significant Teotihuacan influence in Tikal, both culturally and architecturally. His name appears on a stela at Tikal and also at Kaminaljuyu, a site near modern Guatemala City. He probably died about 420. Yax Nuun Ahiin I had no successor named on the monuments of Tikal until much later.
During his reign, the city's central park was reconfigured, and a number of the buildings were repaired or expanded.

In the early 7th century , Caracol seems to have again attacked and defeated Tikal , causing great destruction and " termination deposits " ( elaborate destruction of artifacts in a limited area ) and Tikal 's power did n't recover until the late 7th century .
In the 9th century , Caracol was abandoned , at the time of the Classic Maya Collapse , which is still not fully understood .
This adds to the body of evidence that many Maya cities collapsed due to environmental degradation and agricultural exhaustion , exacerbated by the effects of climate change , and warfare .
This may be true , but it is also important to consider the role of other factors like trade disruptions and the fragmentation of the Maya polity .
The cause of the Classic Maya collapse remains one of the biggest mysteries of archaeology , and no consensus yet exists among scholars .
